Why Abilene businesses miss calls

Abilene is home to Dyess Air Force Base and three private universities: Abilene Christian, Hardin-Simmons and McMurry. Education and health care employ almost 30% of workers, and retail over 13%. Base transfers and the school calendar bring waves of new residents, while ranch and small-town customers often drive in from the Big Country. Many local firms run small teams, so calls stack up quickly.

Which Abilene businesses benefit most?

  • Medical offices: Patients from nearby towns can book at any hour.
  • Real estate agents: Air Force families on orders often call from out of state.
  • Auto repair shops: Book visits while your team stays in the bays.

Can you keep your Abilene phone number?

Yes. Abilene callers will usually see the 325 area codes, and you can keep the number customers already know. Everything is set up remotely, so you do not need new equipment or a visit to an office.

What to check before you go live

  1. Test real calls: ask awkward questions, not only easy ones, and listen to how it handles them.
  2. Set the rules: decide which calls transfer to a person and which become messages.
  3. Plan your minutes: estimate your busiest month, not an average one.
  4. Tell callers what you need to: Texas is generally treated as a one-party consent state for recording calls, but rules differ for callers in other states, so check with your advisor if you record calls.
